target.title: fix(googlechat): keep accounts.default streaming when doctor migrates named accounts
target.body:
Closes #105940

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor --fix` could drop an inherited Google Chat `accounts.default.blockStreaming` setting when migrating a named account that only had a flat streaming key such as `chunkMode`. Runtime then treated the named account's partial `streaming` object as a wholesale replacement, so block streaming silently turned off for that account.

## Why This Change Was Made

Google Chat named-account resolution layers `accounts.default` before the named account and replaces `streaming` wholesale (same inheritance shape as WhatsApp). The generic root-only seeding path (`accountStreamingReplacesRoot`) only copied channel-root streaming into newly materialized account objects and never consulted `accounts.default`.

This mirrors the WhatsApp plugin-local `seedMigratedAccountStreaming` repair from #105709: migrate flat aliases, then deep-fill missing fields from `accounts.default` (falling back to root) for accounts that did not already have a nested `streaming` object.

## User Impact

Multi-account Google Chat configs that shared block-streaming (or other delivery settings) via `accounts.default` keep those settings after `openclaw doctor --fix`, instead of losing them when a named account also had a flat streaming key to migrate.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/googlechat/src/doctor-contract.test.ts` → 6 passed
  - includes regression: `accounts.default.blockStreaming` + named `chunkMode` retains both after migration
  - includes case-insensitive `accounts.Default` seeding
  - existing root-seeding and legacy streamMode/group allow cases still pass
- No competing open PRs for #105940 at open time
